title: Cracking Cheese
summary: A personal design manifesto told through one metaphor from outside design. It argues that ideas get better with age, written as a guide to ripening cheese.
coverAlt: Poster of a wheel of cheese with the manifesto set around its rind

blocks.heading: The idea
blocks.body: Students rush ideas to critique. Cheese teaches patience. A good idea needs time, the right conditions, and someone to turn it now and then.

blocks.caption: The manifesto set around the rind, one line for each stage of ripening.

blocks.heading: Process
blocks.body: The manifesto began as two pages and ended as five lines. I photographed the cheese myself and set the text around the rind, so you turn the poster to read it, the way a cheesemaker turns a wheel.

blocks.label: Photo shoot. Lighting tests and the cheeses that didn’t make it.

blocks.heading: Reflection
blocks.body: Critique asked whether the joke would bury the idea. Plain, careful typography kept it serious enough to be read.
